title: Release traffic decoupling brain dump
body:
Notes to self - rough, do not share as-is

Context:
- Trying to land a safer path for model variant rollouts without relying on single global traffic split. Want per-customer and per-region decoupling plus a holdback cohort for longer tail signal.
- Goal: reduce noisy rollouts from sudden client-driven token spikes and let KV/cache warmups happen per-variant before full cutover.

High level approach (sketch):
1) Shadow stage (T0): route 100% production requests still to current default; shadow to candidate variant in parallel but do not count for latency SLOs or billing. Output capture for eval.
2) Micro-probe stage (T1): small synthetic + low-risk client cohort (0.1-1% global) diverted to candidate, observe latency/err/quality windows. Allow gradient traffic ramp locally per region.
3) Gradual-stagger stage (T2): increase traffic by geometric factor (x3) every 6h to a cap per-region. Use sticky cohorts to avoid flapping.
4) Holdback cohort (TH): keep 5-10% of users pinned to baseline for at least 48h after reaching 50% global traffic to catch regressions in long-tail usage.
5) Full cutover (TF): if pass metrics for 72h, promote candidate to default and convert holdback into canary-for-next.

Quick checklist (operational):
- [ ] Create experiment config: per-region caps, cohort selectors, sticky cookie TTL, rollout window.
- [ ] Deploy routing config to staging cluster; validate control-plane UI shows new variant and split rules.
- [ ] Instrument shadow logging for pairwise output diff store (request id to baseline/candidate).
- [ ] Warm KV cache by replaying top-10k prefixes (best-effort, background).
- [ ] Pre-create rollback image/tag and pin policy for immediate revert.
- [ ] Add ephemeral RBAC for on-call to adjust splits within 1 min via console.

Telemetry / metrics to watch (first 30m, next 24h):
- infra: p95/p99 latency token-level, tail latency by model variant and region, GPU utilization and memory footprint.
- errors: 5xx rate, OOM events, internal-runtime-exceptions, grpc timeouts.
- quality: generation perplexity proxies, eval-suite regressions on golden prompt set, automated A/B user scoring (if available).
- cost: tokens/sec by variant, unexpected burst billing alerts.
- traffic: percent-of-requests per-cohort, sticky churn, client retry loops detected.

Safety thresholds (auto and manual):
- immediate rollback triggers (auto): p99 latency > baseline.p99 * 2 for 5 consecutive min OR error-rate increase > 2x baseline for 3 min OR GPU OOM spike.
- pause ramp triggers (auto): sustained p95 increase > baseline.p95 * 1.5 for 15m OR quality regression on golden set (delta > threshold).
- manual review triggers: any customer-reported hallucination severity > medium for top 10 customers in holdback cohort.

Rollback playbook (quick):
- 00: Confirm alerts (heap/metrics/diff store).
- 01: Move traffic splits to baseline for affected regions via console (use emergency-presets).
- 02: Relaunch baseline variant if in degraded state; if config issue, rollback config repo PR and redeploy router.
- 03: Collect pairwise example set from diff store for postmortem.
- 04: Notify on-call, product-safety, and affected account owners (template in Confluence).
- 05: Open postmortem ticket (link to RINF-2345 for tracking).

Experiment design notes (data collection):
- Keep full request/response pairs for shadowed requests for 7 days (default retention), store hashes for privacy-sensitive fields.
- Compute pairwise similarity metrics (levenshtein / embedding cosine) offline nightly. Flag top 1% deltas for manual review.
- Use synthetic probes for rare prefix coverage - run every 4h from each region.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to enforce per-customer spend guardrails when candidate variant has different token emission profile? (need billing hook)
- Sticky cohorts: cookie vs client-id vs API-key? cookie unreliable for SDK users. Prefer API-key pinning but must handle key rotation.
- Is 5-10% holdback big enough to catch low-frequency regressions for large corp customers? maybe use stratified sampling by customer ARR.
- Validate retention/privacy reqs for storing shadow outputs for enterprise customers. Might need opt-out flag.

Quick commands / knobs (notes for console ops):
- emergency-presets: name=rollout-stop, splits={baseline:100} (applies regionally)
- ramp script: ./tools/ramp-traffic --variant candidateA --factor 3 --interval 6h --regions us-east,eu-west
- diff export: ./tools/export-diffs --since 2026-02-27 --variant candidateA --out /tmp/diffs.tgz

Postmortem checklist (if rollback):
- run pairwise-diff analysis, tag top-10 contributing prompts
- correlate with mem/CPU/GPU events during windows (use observability trace ids)
- interview on-call and product-safety, capture decisions and timeline
- propose mitigation: improved pre-promote test, stricter auto-throttle, or larger holdback cohort

Next steps (for me):
- sync with Raj + Sofia next Thu to review thresholds and cohort selectors (Slack DM sent).
- prototype shadow diff collector in staging (PR 1892 referenced above) - refine retention policy with security.
- sketch console UX for per-customer pinned holdback toggle (low-fidelity mock).

Random notes / heuristics I keep forgetting:
- warmup matters: first 10k requests after a variant becomes non-shadow often have elevated latency until KV caches stabilized. plan for a "soft-warmup" period where candidate is allowed slightly higher latency without auto-rollback.
- prefer multi-dimensional rollback rules (latency+errors) to avoid flip-flopping on noisy single metric.
- document every manual adjustment in the rollout timeline (small note in console helps postmortem).

End of dump.
